channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Villagers help protect elephant migration routes across the India-Nepal border [7/10]
item.description: Elephant herds follow ancestral routes through the Terai passed down across generations, and local communities are working to keep these corridors safe. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led protection of wildlife corridors, though still ongoing.)

item.title: Former doctor stages Bharatanatyam performance by 40 dancers on a Goa beach [6/10]
item.description: An artist brought 40 classical Bharatanatyam dancers to Morjim beach in Goa, combining traditional dance with the coastal landscape. (Goodness 6/10: A pleasant cultural event with local impact.)

item.title: Compound from pomegranates and walnuts may help treat heart failure [6/10]
item.description: Researchers found that urolithin A, a compound the gut makes after eating pomegranates, walnuts and berries, improved heart function by up to 80% in certain types of heart failure with few treatments. (Goodness 6/10: Promising early finding for a hard-to-treat condition.)

item.title: Delhi volunteer group clears large amounts of waste from parks and waterways [6/10]
item.description: A community cleanup initiative in Delhi now has 350 active volunteers who have removed thousands of tonnes of waste from parks, canals and riverbanks. They plan to open an environmental school for children. (Goodness 6/10: A local, citizen-led effort with real results, but limited to one city.)

item.title: Long-running Australian forest study shows thinning can serve timber, wildlife and carbon [7/10]
item.description: A 30-year Australian experiment found that carefully managed forest thinning can support timber production, wildlife habitat and carbon storage at the same time. (Goodness 7/10: Long-term evidence for managing forests for several goals at once.)

item.title: Fishermen rescue newborn elephant calf swept into Teesta River [6/10]
item.description: Fishermen saved a newborn elephant calf carried away by the Teesta River in Jalpaiguri. A veterinarian says the viral embrace was normal elephant social behaviour. (Goodness 6/10: Successful wildlife rescue of one animal.)

item.title: Psychologists advise families on telling children about a rare disease [6/10]
item.description: Child psychologists suggest parents first absorb the shock, then match their language to the child's age and build a support network around the family. (Goodness 6/10: Practical help for families, benefiting a small group.)

item.title: Why Haryana produces so many of India's top wrestlers [6/10]
item.description: Traditional akharas and kushti culture, plus the example of Olympic champions, have built a training ecosystem in Haryana that draws wrestlers from across India. (Goodness 6/10: A strong community sporting tradition, though local in scope.)

item.title: Vitamin D analog may weaken pancreatic tumours' protective shield [6/10]
item.description: A vitamin D analog showed promise in clinical trials for breaking down the defences that protect pancreatic tumours from treatment. (Goodness 6/10: Hopeful for a very hard cancer, but still at trial stage.)

item.title: Temporary shades over Caribbean corals reduce heat damage [7/10]
item.description: Researchers in Florida found that shades placed over vulnerable corals limited harm from warm seawater and partly reversed bleaching. (Goodness 7/10: Promising field result, but still small-scale.)

item.title: Ancient Christian complex in Aleppo reopens after 14 years [6/10]
item.description: A fifth-century Christian heritage site in Aleppo has reopened after landmines were cleared and war and earthquake damage was repaired. (Goodness 6/10: Heritage restored, benefiting one community.)

item.title: Football fan rescues woman trapped chest-deep in mud [6/10]
item.description: A man who left his home in frustration during a match found a woman stuck in mud and helped save her life. (Goodness 6/10: A life saved, though a single local event.)

item.title: Enzyme UBE2N may protect against worsening fatty liver disease [6/10]
item.description: Researchers found the enzyme UBE2N helps liver cells clear damaged mitochondria and break down fat, which could guard against inflammation and scarring. (Goodness 6/10: Promising target for a common disease, but still early research.)

item.title: ESA's Juice probe swings past Earth on its way to Jupiter [6/10]
item.description: The Juice spacecraft used an Earth gravity assist on 28 September to gain 3.5 km/s and change course, testing its instruments on Earth and the Moon. (Goodness 6/10: A smooth milestone for a major science mission.)

item.title: Trial of post-exposure drug begins in DR Congo for Bundibugyo Ebola [6/10]
item.description: A clinical trial has started with 250 people exposed to the rare Bundibugyo variant to test whether a preventive drug can stop infection. (Goodness 6/10: Response effort under way, with results still to come.)

item.title: Project Neev helps 900 rural children catch up in maths and English [6/10]
item.description: A former civil-service aspirant founded a programme using tablet-based learning and local women facilitators to improve children's literacy and numeracy. (Goodness 6/10: Local education help reaching hundreds of children.)

item.title: Uttar Pradesh farmers plant turmeric to keep elephants away from crops [7/10]
item.description: About 100 farmers near Katarniaghat are growing turmeric beside crops elephants like, as a less-attractive buffer that reduces raids. (Goodness 7/10: Low-cost way to ease human-wildlife conflict.)

item.title: Karnataka plans to restore 500 lakes with a 150-crore programme [6/10]
item.description: The state initiative aims to rejuvenate 500 lakes, and the article outlines what indicators show a lake is truly healthy. (Goodness 6/10: Large restoration plan, though results depend on delivery.)

item.title: Four Indian startups turn coconut shells and rice husks into household goods [6/10]
item.description: Startups in India are turning agricultural by-products such as coconut shells and rice husk ash into consumer products including kitchen bowls. (Goodness 6/10: Gives farm waste a second use, still at small scale.)

item.title: Colorado neighborhood of nearly 100 homes uses ground-source heat pumps [7/10]
item.description: Geothermal company Dandelion Energy and homebuilder Lennar completed almost 100 homes with ground-source heat pumps, offering a model for future home energy use. (Goodness 7/10: Real homes built at scale with efficient clean heating.)

item.title: UK national museums will stay free for foreign visitors [6/10]
item.description: After talks with the government, 14 major national museums confirmed they will keep free admission for international visitors. (Goodness 6/10: Keeps culture open to everyone; a continuation rather than a new gain.)

item.title: Probiotic treatment shielded corals from bleaching in Red Sea heat wave [6/10]
item.description: A study found that beneficial bacteria protected corals from bleaching during a marine heat wave, pointing to a possible tool for reef protection. (Goodness 6/10: Promising result, but still an early study at small scale.)

item.title: Tanzanian network grew a $25,000 grant into community-led coastal conservation [6/10]
item.description: The Mwambao Coastal Community Network expanded from a small grant made during the 2008 financial crisis into a broader community-led conservation effort on Tanzania's coast. (Goodness 6/10: Shows local leadership can sustain conservation over time.)

item.title: Deaf dancers in Burkina Faso use vibration technique to follow rhythm [7/10]
item.description: Deaf and hearing-impaired dancers use the Vibra-Signe technique to feel music, giving them a route to social inclusion. (Goodness 7/10: Inclusion for a marginalised group, at community scale.)

item.title: Antarctic wind turbines have saved 122,000 gallons of diesel [6/10]
item.description: Three turbines on Ross Island have powered McMurdo Station for 15 years, cutting fuel shipments and emissions at the research base. (Goodness 6/10: A long-running, proven clean-energy success at small scale.)

item.title: Uganda and conservation group to co-manage park sector home to tree-climbing lions [6/10]
item.description: The Uganda Wildlife Authority and the Wildlife Conservation Society signed a 10-year agreement to jointly manage part of a national park known for its tree-climbing lions. (Goodness 6/10: Long-term management support for wildlife and habitat.)

item.title: NASA's Roman telescope passes key pointing and coronagraph tests [6/10]
item.description: The Roman Space Telescope showed very stable pointing and captured focused images with its coronagraph, an instrument designed to help image planets around other stars. (Goodness 6/10: Solid progress for a flagship observatory.)

item.title: Mobile labs speed up Ebola testing in eastern DR Congo [7/10]
item.description: Mobile testing units placed in treatment centres cut waiting times that previously took up to 72 hours, helping care teams act faster. (Goodness 7/10: Faster diagnosis helps contain outbreaks.)

item.title: Blood cancer stem cells found to depend on NAD for energy [6/10]
item.description: High-risk myelodysplastic syndrome stem cells rely heavily on the molecule NAD, and blocking that pathway weakened them while sparing healthy blood cells in lab tests. (Goodness 6/10: A selective treatment target, still at the lab stage.)

item.title: Solar-powered 'community lighthouses' keep New Orleans lit in blackouts [8/10]
item.description: Faith leaders have set up 14 solar-backed community centres that give neighbours power and help during storms and outages, with plans to spread nationwide. (Goodness 8/10: Practical resilience that protects vulnerable people in disasters.)

item.title: Long COVID, ME/CFS and three other conditions may share biology [6/10]
item.description: A study suggests five fatigue-related conditions disrupt common networks tied to immunity and energy production, which could lead to blood tests and treatments. (Goodness 6/10: Could help many under-served patients, but tests and therapies are not yet here.)

item.title: Urine test could spare many women invasive womb cancer procedures [7/10]
item.description: University of Manchester researchers developed a urine-based screening test that identified most cancers correctly, which could reduce the need for invasive checks. (Goodness 7/10: Gentler diagnosis for many patients, pending wider validation.)

item.title: Lisbon trials sterile male mosquitoes against dengue [6/10]
item.description: Portugal released 30,000 sterile male mosquitoes in Lisbon to study how they spread and compete, testing a pesticide-free way to control dengue. (Goodness 6/10: Promising non-chemical approach, still at trial stage.)

item.title: Decades of clean-up at a closed British Columbia copper mine earn a reclamation award [7/10]
item.description: British Columbia honoured the operators of a closed copper mine for 30 years of land reclamation and environmental monitoring after the site shut down. (Goodness 7/10: Sustained repair of a damaged landscape, though limited to one site.)

item.title: Chemists find cheap way to recycle fats from industrial ice cream waste [6/10]
item.description: Researchers developed an inexpensive base treatment that recovers dairy fats from factory ice cream waste, which could be reused instead of discarded. (Goodness 6/10: Early-stage method that could reduce food-industry waste.)

item.title: Study helps predict how well mangroves protect coasts from storm waves [6/10]
item.description: New research offers methods to estimate how much mangrove forests reduce wave energy in severe storms, supporting coastal climate adaptation planning. (Goodness 6/10: Better tools for nature-based coastal protection.)

item.title: California legalizes plug-in balcony solar panels [7/10]
item.description: Governor Newsom signed a law allowing residents to use plug-in solar panels on balconies, giving renters and apartment dwellers an affordable way to generate power. (Goodness 7/10: Opens clean energy to people who cannot install rooftop solar.)

item.title: Endangered black-faced lion tamarins vaccinated against yellow fever in Brazil [7/10]
item.description: Researchers have vaccinated black-faced lion tamarins in the Atlantic Forest, a first for this critically endangered primate, to protect it from yellow fever outbreaks. (Goodness 7/10: A concrete step to protect a species at risk.)

item.title: The felled Sycamore Gap tree is growing back [7/10]
item.description: Three years after the famous tree on Hadrian's Wall was cut down, aerial images show a ring of vigorous new shoots already about a metre tall. (Goodness 7/10: A heartening recovery, mostly symbolic in scale.)

item.title: German prototype wind turbine taller than the Eiffel Tower [6/10]
item.description: Germany is testing a 365-metre prototype wind turbine intended to raise electricity output from wind power. (Goodness 6/10: Useful clean-energy progress, still a prototype.)

item.title: Chinese reactor reports fusion using hydrogen-boron fuel [6/10]
item.description: Engineers at a commercial fusion company say they achieved fusion with hydrogen-boron, a fuel that produces almost no neutron radiation. (Goodness 6/10: Promising for clean energy, but still an early lab milestone far from a power plant.)

item.title: Fire survivors replant LA's burned hills with seed bombs [7/10]
item.description: Residents who lost homes in the fires made and handed out 10,000 balls of native seeds to help the landscape recover. (Goodness 7/10: Community healing plus ecological recovery.)

item.title: Two new giant stick insect species described in Australia [6/10]
item.description: Researchers identified two new Australian stick insects, one laying unusual lidded eggs, and showed a long-recognised species had been misidentified for decades. (Goodness 6/10: Adds to knowledge of biodiversity worth protecting.)

item.title: Protective fabric more than triples strawberry yields [7/10]
item.description: A crop covering raised strawberry harvests up to 3.5 times while keeping pests out and cutting pesticide use. (Goodness 7/10: More food with fewer chemicals.)

item.title: Kenyan conservation shifts toward community-led conservancies [6/10]
item.description: Conservationist Dickson Kaelo describes how pastoralist communities in Kenya are gaining decision-making power over wildlife in community conservancies. (Goodness 6/10: Positive model for local control, shown through an interview.)

item.title: Arabian Sea humpbacks confirmed as a distinct subspecies [6/10]
item.description: Genetic analysis shows the isolated, non-migrating whales of the Arabian Sea are genetically distinct, which strengthens the case for targeted protection. (Goodness 6/10: Useful for conservation, but mainly a scientific finding.)

item.title: MIND diet linked to slower brain shrinkage [7/10]
item.description: People who closely followed the MIND diet showed less brain shrinkage and grey matter loss, roughly equal to 2.5 fewer years of brain ageing. (Goodness 7/10: Accessible, low-cost habit with a measurable brain benefit, though observational.)

item.title: Stolen Greek antiquities spanning 5,000 years go home [6/10]
item.description: New York authorities returned a large haul of looted Greek objects, including bronze helmets and sculptures as old as 2,700 BCE. (Goodness 6/10: Restores cultural heritage to its country of origin.)

item.title: Cutting ultra-processed food eased depression symptoms in a small trial [6/10]
item.description: In preliminary testing, people with depression who sharply reduced ultra-processed food reported notable improvements, possibly linked to less gut damage and inflammation. (Goodness 6/10: Encouraging and practical, but early and small.)

item.title: Damage from the main Alzheimer's risk gene may be reversible [7/10]
item.description: Researchers found how the APOE4 gene harms brain blood vessels and partly reversed the effect in experiments. (Goodness 7/10: Opens a new treatment path; still early-stage research.)

item.title: Unsupported arm can inflate blood pressure readings by about 7 points [6/10]
item.description: Johns Hopkins researchers found that leaving the arm unsupported during a check raised systolic readings by around 6.5 mmHg, enough to affect diagnoses. (Goodness 6/10: Simple, immediately usable fix to improve care for many.)

item.title: Argentina runs Latin America's first solar-powered train [7/10]
item.description: A battery-electric train powered by solar energy and regenerative braking now serves the Quebrada de Humahuaca route in the Andes. (Goodness 7/10: Clean transport on a historic route, on a small scale.)

item.title: Inuit bear guards use traditional knowledge to protect Arctic communities [6/10]
item.description: Training programmes in northern Labrador combine Inuit knowledge with specialised instruction so communities can handle polar bears appearing in new places. (Goodness 6/10: Community-led safety that also supports coexistence with wildlife.)

item.title: Well-preserved Gobi Desert fossil sheds new light on early mammal evolution [6/10]
item.description: A fossil found in Mongolia challenges earlier ideas about how mammals evolved while dinosaurs were still alive. (Goodness 6/10: New knowledge about our deep past, though limited in everyday impact.)

item.title: Actor's video helps bonded rescue dogs get adopted [6/10]
item.description: Actor Chris Evans made a promotional video for two bonded dogs at a Boston shelter, and a family adopted both soon afterwards. (Goodness 6/10: Small but happy outcome for two animals.)

item.title: English golf course turned into a seabird wetland [7/10]
item.description: A former coastal golf course has been rewilded into wetland habitat now used by plovers, terns and other birds. (Goodness 7/10: Real habitat gain for threatened coastal birds.)

item.title: Sea turtles nest on California beaches for the first time on record [7/10]
item.description: Olive ridley turtles laid eggs on Southern California sand, the first nesting ever documented on the US West Coast and a sign the species is widening its range. (Goodness 7/10: A first-ever wildlife milestone, though partly tied to warming seas.)

item.title: Paying for wildlife photos turns hunters into protectors [8/10]
item.description: Villages in Indonesia earn money for camera evidence of living animals instead of hunting them, helping orangutans and rare birds. (Goodness 8/10: A working incentive model that changes behaviour and protects species.)

item.title: Norway creates a large new marine protected area for whales and seabirds [8/10]
item.description: The Andfjorden reserve covers roughly 714 square miles of rich northern waters used by whales, seabirds and cold-water reefs. (Goodness 8/10: Durable protection over a large area of ocean.)

item.title: Denver opens housing for homeless college students [7/10]
item.description: A nonprofit and local universities now offer up to two years of subsidised housing and support to students without a stable home. (Goodness 7/10: Directly changes the odds for students at risk of dropping out.)
